subject: Chemistry
title: Particles of Matter
summary: Matter looks continuous, but it is made of extremely small particles. Two crystals of potassium permanganate can colour glass after glass of water.
keyPoints: Matter is **not continuous**: it is made of very tiny **particles**.
The particles are far too small to see, even with an ordinary microscope.
KMnO₄ activity: the colour stays visible after many dilutions.
A few crystals contain a huge number of particles.

blocks.alt: Six glasses of potassium permanganate solution, each lighter than the last
blocks.caption: Each glass is lighter, yet still coloured.

list: Dissolve 2–3 crystals of potassium permanganate in about 100 mL of water: deep purple.
Take 10 mL of it into 90 mL of clear water.
Take 10 mL of the new solution into another 90 mL of water.
Repeat 5–8 times: the water is still coloured.

blocks.p: A few crystals contain a **very large number of very small particles**, which keep spreading out into every glass. So matter is made of particles, and they are extremely small.

list: Sugar dissolves and the water level hardly rises: its particles fit into the spaces between water particles.
A few drops of Dettol or ink spread their smell or colour through a whole glass.

blocks.p: **Common mistakes:** the colour disappears on dilution (it gets lighter but stays visible); particles are dust-sized (they are far smaller).

quiz.q: In the KMnO₄ activity, after many dilutions the water:
quiz.explain: The colour gets lighter but stays visible, because a few crystals hold a huge number of tiny particles.

quiz.q: The activity shows that particles of matter are:
quiz.explain: A few crystals colour a lot of water, so there must be a huge number of very small particles.

quiz.q: Why does the water level hardly rise when sugar dissolves?
options: Sugar particles fit into spaces between water particles
quiz.explain: Sugar particles occupy the spaces between the water particles.

quiz.q: Can we see the particles of matter with an ordinary microscope?
options: No, they are far too small
quiz.explain: They are much smaller than anything an ordinary microscope can show.
